title: The night song
hookLine: Sohila means song of praise; its five hymns close the day and close a life
carry: a song of joy, for the last night

lines: A GRANDMOTHER HUMMING IN THE DARK.
THE LAST THING HEARD BEFORE SLEEP.
THE NIGHT SONG GETS THE FINAL WORD.
cards: A lot of homes have a bedtime song. A grandmother humming in the dark. A father singing the same three lines every night, badly, because the baby likes them.

The words matter less than the fact that they're the last thing heard before sleep. The day has a lot of voices in it; the night song gets the final word. Sikhs have one too, and it's sung not only at the end of a day.

teach.h: SOHILA: A SONG OF PRAISE, OF JOY.
teach.b: It's called Kirtan Sohila, or simply Sohila. Sohila is usually explained as a song of praise, and in old Punjabi it was also a word for joyful songs, the kind sung at weddings.
It's short: five shabads, on pages twelve and thirteen of the Guru Granth Sahib, right after Rehras. The first three are by Guru Nanak, the fourth by Guru Ram Das, the fifth by Guru Arjan.

teach.h: BEFORE SLEEP, AND AT THE CREMATION.
teach.b: The Sikh code of conduct places it at night, before sleep. Some say it in bed with the light off, or play it softly as children fall asleep. And it closes more than a day.

In gurdwaras, Kirtan Sohila is recited when the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest at night. When a Sikh dies, it's recited at the cremation, followed by Ardas. The same five hymns at bedtime and at a funeral.

teach.h: SLEEP AND DEATH: HANDED BACK IN CALM.
teach.b: Some Sikh teachers describe sleep and death as both a kind of letting go, a handing of yourself back to the One, and the night song meets both with the same calm.
The first hymn even speaks of a day fixed in advance, the way a wedding date is written, and friends gathering to bless the one setting out.
Over the next two weeks we'll take the five hymns one at a time, sound first, then meaning.

how: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila at night before sleep, often in bed; it is recited when the Guru Granth Sahib is put to rest in many gurdwaras and at the cremation of a Sikh, followed by Ardas.

o: a song of praise and joy, sung before sleep
a lullaby sung only to put small children to sleep
a lament sung by mourners at the end of a life

the same five hymns close a day and a life.

games.q: a Sikh family has gathered at a cremation. which bani is recited there, before Ardas?
games.why: the same five hymns said at bedtime are recited at the cremation: sleep and death both handed back with calm.

practice: Lie back or sit loosely, and let your body grow heavy, as if night has already come. Let one line you've learned on this path be the last thing you hear, anand bhaiaa, or hamree karo haath dai rachhaa, said once, slowly.
If you'd like, Kirtan Sohila is in any gutka or recording, and takes only a few minutes.

wordCard.voice: Sohila. Kirtan Sohila, the Sikh night song: five shabads of praise said before sleep, and recited at the end of a life.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sohilaa, a song of praise or joy; Kirtan Sohila is the Sikh night prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: a song of joy, for the last night. The same calm meets both. Day four hundred twenty-one.
